Main charitable entity types: NGOs under Law No. 06/L-043 on Freedom of Association in NGOs (2019, amended by Law No. 08/L-244, 2024): association (3+ founders), foundation (1+ founder, EUR 1,000 initial capital) and institute (1+ founder, non-membership) (Arts. 16-19); foreign/international NGOs register a Kosovo branch (Art. 24); all registered by the Department for Registration and Liaison with NGOs (DRLNGO), Ministry of Internal Affairs (MPB); optional public beneficiary status (Art. 37).
Key local requirements: Foreign natural/legal persons may found an NGO (Art. 3(1.7)); association needs 3+ founders, foundation/institute 1+; foundation needs EUR 1,000 initial capital; authorized representative must be an adult resident of Kosovo (Arts. 3(1.8), 23(4)); Kosovo seat/address; documents: act of establishment, statute, ID copies of founders and representative, registration certificate for legal-person founders (Art. 22(4)); foreign branch: notarized proof of legal personality abroad, Kosovo branch address, head-office representative declaration (Art. 24); filings in Albanian or Serbian (official languages).
Est. cost & time: Government fee: none published (no fee in Law 06/L-043); realistic all-in EUR 300-1,000 (~USD 350-1,150) for translation/notarisation of foreign documents, statute drafting and a local representative/lawyer, plus EUR 1,000 capital for a foundation; statutory decision within 45 days (Art. 25(2) as amended by 08/L-244), 1-3 months end-to-end.
Notes: Law No. 06/L-043 (Official Gazette No. 11/2019, 24.04.2019) repealed Law No. 04/L-057; amended by Law No. 08/L-244 (Official Gazette 05.01.2024) which lengthened the registration decision period from 30 to 45 days and set a EUR 50 fine on the authorized representative for not reporting changes | implementing rules: Administrative Instruction (GRK) No. 12/2022 on registration and functioning of NGOs, amended by AI (GRK) No. 02/2025 (45-day review confirmed) | 2019 law removed the old bar on foreign residents as founders and added the 'institute' form | incomplete applications get 15 days to cure (Art. 25(4)-(5)) | foreign documents (e.g. a branch's proof of legal personality) need notarisation plus certified Albanian/Serbian translation | NGO department moved from the Ministry of Public Administration to the Ministry of Internal Affairs in the 2021 reorganisation.
Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): The NGO's authorized representative must be a Kosovo resident (Law 06/L-043 Arts. 3(1.8), 23(4)), so a remote Australian founder needs a trusted local representative.
Registration fee (USD): none (no state fee in Law 06/L-043 or AI 12/2022; Global Philanthropy Environment Index reports USD 0)
Time to register: 6 weeks-3 months (45-day statutory decision period under Art. 25(2) as amended by Law 08/L-244)
Charitable deduction regime: Individuals (taxed on real-income basis) and companies may deduct donations/sponsorship for humanitarian, health, education, religious, scientific, cultural, environmental and sports purposes up to 10% of taxable income (CIT Law No. 06/L-105; PIT law), plus up to a further 10% for areas set by special laws; receipts signed and stamped by the beneficiary required; donations to public-beneficiary-status NGOs qualify.
Foreign donor / donation restrictions: None notable (no foreign-agent or foreign-funding register); AML rules limit NGO cash receipts/disbursements (EUR 500 per source per day, EUR 5,000 per source per year) and require suspicious-transaction reports to the Financial Intelligence Unit.
Annual compliance & reporting: Public-beneficiary-status NGOs file an annual report (management, activities, financial statements, auditor's report where required) by 31 March (Art. 38), extendable 30 days; independent audit if annual income/expenses exceed EUR 100,000 (Art. 38(8)); missing reports lead to suspension then revocation of status (Art. 39); all NGOs must report changes within 30 days (fines EUR 50-250 on the NGO/authorized representative under Art. 29 as amended); NGOs also file tax returns with the Tax Administration of Kosovo (ATK).
Tax-exempt status & benefits: Not automatic: public beneficiary status (Art. 37) is requested at registration or later for principal activities such as humanitarian aid, education, health, human rights; DRLNGO decides within 45 days; benefits are CIT exemption on income used for public-benefit purposes and tax/fiscal relief (e.g. immovable property tax); non-PBS NGOs pay 10% CIT on profits; revoked status can be re-sought only after 2 years.
Bank account (remote feasibility): Needs a local visit: Kosovo banks (ProCredit, Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo, TEB, NLB Prishtina) require account holders and authorised signatories to appear at a branch with valid ID and proof of address for KYC; a non-resident-founded NGO also presents its DRLNGO registration certificate and fiscal number, and banks apply enhanced AML due diligence to NGOs and foreign beneficial owners - a resident authorized representative can usually handle it.
